faq.q: How long are offshore wind turbine blades?
faq.a: The biggest are over 100 metres long, longer than Big Ben's tower is tall, and are made from glass and carbon fibre in one piece. They are carried out to sea on special ships.
asks: How big is a wind turbine blade?

faq.q: Why are wind turbines getting bigger?
faq.a: A rotor twice as wide sweeps four times the area and catches four times as much wind, and taller towers reach faster, steadier wind. Fewer, bigger turbines also need fewer foundations and cables.
asks: Why not use lots of small wind turbines?

faq.q: How much power does one offshore turbine make?
faq.a: The largest offshore turbines are rated at around 13 to 15 megawatts, and some newer ones even more. Over a year, one can make enough electricity for many thousands of homes.
asks: How many homes can a wind turbine power?

faq.q: How fast do the blade tips move?
faq.a: The rotor turns slowly, only about 5 to 10 times a minute, but the tips travel round a huge circle, so they move at nearly 300 kilometres an hour.
asks: How fast do wind turbines spin?

faq.a: Land turbines must be carried along roads, under bridges and round corners, and must not tower too far over homes. At sea, ships can carry much bigger parts.
asks: Why are land wind turbines shorter?

facts: GE's Haliade-X offshore wind turbine has blades 107 metres long.
The area a rotor sweeps grows with the square of its blade length, so doubling the blade length quadruples the area.

quiz.say: A designer doubles the blade length of a wind turbine. Roughly how much more area do the blades sweep?
quiz.show: Double the blade length: swept area grows…
quiz.why: The swept area is a circle, and a circle's area grows with the radius squared: two squared is four.

wrong.1: Area grows faster than length; it goes with the square.
wrong.2: Eight would be a cube; a circle's area goes with the square.
